questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup:
Statement (I): Muller - Breslau principle is an axiom that can be established using the principle of virtual work.
Statement (II): A body subjected to an imaginary virtual motion will experience zero work due to all forces and moments acting on the body.
questions.questionText: Statement (I): Muller - Breslau principle is an axiom that can be established using the principle of virtual work. Statement (II): A body subjected to an imaginary virtual motion will experience zero work due to all forces and moments acting on the body.

options.html: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true and Statement (II) is the correct explanation of Statement (I).
options.text: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true and Statement (II) is the correct explanation of Statement (I).

options.html: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true but Statement (II) is not the correct explanation of Statement (I).
options.text: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are true but Statement (II) is not the correct explanation of Statement (I).

options.html: Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false.
options.text: Statement (I) is true but Statement (II) is false.

options.html: Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true.
options.text: Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true.

questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
An axiom is something that is self-proved and does not require any specific proof. However,
Muller – Breslau principle is required to be proved using principle of virtual work for its correctness.
Hence Statement (I) is false but Statement (II) is true.
Statement (I) would have been true had the word axiom not been there.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: In a plane truss, counter brace is the member:
questions.questionText: In a plane truss, counter brace is the member:

options.html: that is designed to resist compressive force only.
options.text: that is designed to resist compressive force only.

options.html: that is designed to resist tensile force only.
options.text: that is designed to resist tensile force only.

options.html: that is designed to resist compression and shear.
options.text: that is designed to resist compression and shear.

options.html: that is designed to resist both tension and compression.
options.text: that is designed to resist both tension and compression.

questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
A counter brace in a plane truss is a member designed to resist both tensile and compressive
forces, depending on the load conditions and the direction of the applied forces. In a truss, some
members are designed primarily for tension (ties) and others for compression (struts). However,
a counter brace is specifically included to handle stress reversals that can occur due to varying
load conditions (e.g., live loads, wind loads).
